correctness.rationale: The block-cut incidence tree is unique for every finite cactus; for distinct blocks the endpoint distances are independent uniforms on lengths equal to full bridge length or half circle circumference. Their convolution is continuous piecewise affine. Same-block bridge contributions are continuous, and same-block circle densities alone have negative jumps at half circumference, of exact size 2c/L² each. The total density near zero is 2/L. All cases and knot conventions are established analytically in RESULT.md; exact-rational spot checks and independent simulation supplement the proof.

value.rationale: One natural scalar metric-measure observable recovers a complete weighted cycle-length spectrum and the first Betti number across all positive-length cactus graphs, despite arbitrary bridge architecture and exact jump collisions. This is a substantive natural metric-topological inverse invariant, not a reconstruction of the entire graph or a mere expectation calculation. The explicit full distribution and tree/non-tree criterion provide meaningful structural boundaries for metric-graph shape statistics.
